title: Superposition, interference and coherence
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W06-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; W06-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; W06-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; W06-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: W06-1#N.2a, W06-1#N.8, W06-1#N.9, W06-1#N.12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Constructive interference
items.clue: Meeting in step, crest on crest, so the amplitudes add; heard as loud.

items.label: Path difference
items.clue: Extra distance from one source compared with the other: 0.60 m for 3.00 m and 3.60 m.

items.label: Destructive interference
items.clue: Meeting out of step so that displacements cancel, as when one route is 1.5λ longer; heard as quiet.

items.label: Principle of superposition
items.clue: States that the resultant displacement where waves overlap is the sum of the individual displacements.

questions.stem: Two pulses of identical shape and size but opposite displacement travel towards each other along a stretched string. At one instant they overlap exactly and the whole string is momentarily straight. Which statement about this instant, and what follows it, is correct?

options.text: The pulses have cancelled each other out; the string stays straight from now on.
The string is straight but moving; the pulses then emerge and continue past each other.
The string is straight and at rest; the pulses' energy has become internal energy of the string.
The pulses have collided; each then travels back the way it came, with its shape restored.

questions.stem: Two loudspeakers connected to the same signal generator emit sound in phase at a frequency of 500 Hz. The speed of sound in air is 340 m s⁻¹. At which of these path differences is the sound quiet because of destructive interference?
questions.explanation: λ = 0.68 m, and 1.02 m = 1.5λ, a half-odd number of wavelengths: crest meets trough, destructive.

questions.stem: Two loudspeakers side by side are driven by two separate signal generators, each set to 500 Hz. A listener walking across the room hears no steady pattern of loud and quiet places. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Sound waves from two different sources pass through each other without superposing.
A steady pattern forms only if the listener is the same distance from both speakers.
The phase difference drifts, as two generators never match frequency exactly.
Sources must emit at exactly the same amplitude, and two speakers never do.

questions.explanation: Separate generators differ slightly in frequency, so the phase difference keeps changing and the loud and quiet places move. The sources are not coherent.

questions.stem: Two dippers vibrating in phase act as coherent sources S₁ and S₂ on a ripple tank, producing waves of wavelength 2.0 cm. Point P is 31.0 cm from S₁ and 37.0 cm from S₂. What kind of interference occurs at P?

options.text: Destructive: the paths are 15.5λ and 18.5λ, not whole numbers of λ
Destructive: the path difference, 3λ, is an odd number of λ
Neither: maxima occur only where P is equidistant from S₁ and S₂
Constructive: the path difference is 6.0 cm, which is 3λ
